draft.rationale: This session keeps the committed 15 minute Concept Mapping route and uses the current objective as a tight novice check. The work stays on the order and locations of the three cellular respiration stages, with one memory attempt, one map connection, one evidence check, and one repair.

coverage.focus: Order and locations of glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain in cellular respiration.
essentialIdeas: The stages of cellular respiration go glycolysis, then the Krebs cycle, then the electron transport chain.
Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm, the Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondrial matrix, and the electron transport chain happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
completionEvidence: Attempt each target without notes and correct any exposed gap

methodBriefing.name: Concept Mapping
methodBriefing.what: You will first try to recall the stages and locations from memory, then connect them with exact relationship phrases, check the evidence, and repair any gap.
methodBriefing.why: This fits a novice conceptual-learning check because it exposes whether the sequence and cell locations are linked correctly, not just recognized separately.
how: Answer the first prompt without notes.
Build the named concept links using the location of each stage.
Check the evidence prompt against the completed answer.
Repair only the part that is wrong, then restate the corrected relation.
methodBriefing.completion: The session is complete when you have attempted the required retrieval, made the concept connections, answered the evidence check, and finished the repair attempt if needed.
personalization: YOVA is using the current task and session objective as the starting point until your completed work provides more evidence.

activities.label: Try
activities.title: Order from memory
activities.body: Without notes, name the three main stages in order.
activities.concept: Order of the main stages of cellular respiration
activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis, then the Krebs cycle, then the electron transport chain.
activities.feedback: Check the sequence, not the locations. The key idea is the flow from glucose breakdown to later ATP production.

activities.label: Map
activities.title: Connect each stage to its location
activities.body: Link the stages to their cell locations.

methodRuntime.instructions: Connect the named concepts with relationship phrases.

connections.prompt: Where does the Krebs cycle happen?
connections.expectedRelationship: The Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondrial matrix.

connections.prompt: Where does the electron transport chain happen?
connections.expectedRelationship: The electron transport chain happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

activities.concept: Locations of glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain
activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm. The Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondrial matrix. The electron transport chain happens on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
activities.feedback: Use exact location phrases for each stage. The decisive link is stage plus where it occurs inside the cell.

activities.label: Check
activities.title: Match the evidence
activities.body: Which claim matches the required retrieval evidence for this session?
activities.concept: Order of the main stages of cellular respiration
choices: Say the three stages in order from memory.
activities.correctAnswer: Say the three stages in order from memory.
activities.feedback: The completion evidence is a closed-note recall of the sequence, so the correct choice must name the stages in order rather than only identify one stage.

activities.label: Repair
activities.title: Fix one gap
activities.body: If any part was off, rewrite just the corrected stage or location.

teaching.keyIdea: Repair should target only the exposed gap.
teaching.explanation: If the order was wrong, correct only the sequence. If a location was wrong, correct only that stage-location pair. Keep the rest unchanged so the final answer shows the repaired link clearly.

example.setup: A learner says the Krebs cycle comes before glycolysis.
steps: Replace it with glycolysis first, then the Krebs cycle, then the electron transport chain.
Keep the location claims the same if they were already correct.
example.takeaway: Repair the specific error, not the whole topic.

commonMistake.mistake: Changing every part of the answer after one miss.
commonMistake.correction: Keep the correct parts and fix only the broken link or stage.
